test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 23 Nov, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: In cricket, which of the following is considered as LBW?

options.text: The fielder catches a batted ball on the fly.
The batsman’s body interferes with a bowled ball that would hit the wicket.
The bowler knocks over (or, breaks) the wicket with a bowl.
The fielder catches a ground ball and throws it at the wicket, knocking it down before the batsman gets there.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The batsman's body interferes with a bowled ball that would hit the wicket.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• LBW stands for **Leg Before Wicket**.
 
• An LBW decision is given when the batsman's body (excluding the hand) blocks a ball that would have gone on to hit the stumps.
 
• The ball must pitch in line with the stumps or on the off side for an LBW to be given.
 
• There are various conditions and interpretations by the umpire to determine if the ball would have hit the wicket.
 
• LBW is one of the ways a batsman can be dismissed in cricket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bowled**

 
 
• This occurs when the bowler delivers the ball and it hits the stumps, dislodging the bails.
 
• The batsman is out bowled if the ball hits the stumps directly or after touching the bat or body.
 
 
 
• **Caught**
 
 
• A batsman is out caught if a fielder catches the ball on the full after it has hit the bat or the gloves holding the bat.
 
• This can occur anywhere on the field, including the boundary.
 
 
 
• **Run Out**
 
 
• A batsman is run out if at any time while the ball is in play, no part of his bat or body is grounded behind the popping crease and his wicket is fairly put down by the opposing side.
 
• This usually occurs when attempting a run between wickets.
